@copilot Update this stacked PR directly with the missing regression coverage from the original assignment. The initial implementation is delivered at 53c23ba4d57dc892ed326ab82f85ff369ef664cc and its Copilot review reports no issues, but the actual PR diff does not cover asynchronous delivery or application-owned collisions under customized enrichment keys.

Add focused coverage using the existing library asyncAppenderTest suite, which already targets Logback versions with AsyncAppender support. Exercise actual asynchronous delivery after the MDC appender has enriched an event. Verify that application output still sees the enriched values after the producer span/baggage scopes end and producer MDC is cleared or changed, while OTLP capture selects the original application-owned MDC through the mapper reader. Keep the existing downstream-AsyncAppender correlation limitation and warning behavior; do not assert or implement new asynchronous trace propagation. Use deterministic synchronization and exact exported-attribute assertions, not sleeps or immediate reads of an unsynchronized ListAppender. Add only the test dependency/wiring necessary within the existing suite, without creating an additional suite or changing dependency-version coverage.

In the existing library MDC export tests, add representative application-owned collisions under customized trace/span/flags key names. Configure the MDC appender with those names and run with a real current span and baggage. Verify the configured MDC capture selector preserves the original application values, while application appenders retain their intended enrichment. Keep cases independent where the existing trace-id-present shortcut would otherwise bypass enrichment and mask the span/flags overwrite path. The current doesNotExportEnrichmentWithoutApplicationMdc case only checks a custom trace-id key with no application MDC and does not establish collision preservation.

Keep the current production changes, original-MDC retention, shared mapper callback reuse, serialization compatibility, logger-context preservation, starter coverage, and other tests unchanged unless the new regression reveals a concrete in-scope defect. Do not redesign the production implementation solely for these tests, add global callback hooks, change the parent #21223, or reintroduce baggage-log-record-processor configuration/documentation/tests. This is completion of the originally requested library/starter fix, not a new feature.

Apply the narrowest applicable spotlessApply task directly before behavioral validation. Run the focused baseline/latest-dependency library MDC export tests and existing asyncAppenderTest suite where feasible. Commit the focused corrections to this PR's verified head repository open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation and branch copilot/fix-logback-mdc-export-isolation, retaining base copilot/java-agent-logback-change. Keep the branch assigned by GitHub Copilot cloud agent; do not rename it or create a replacement branch. If GitHub creates a platform-assigned follow-up branch, keep that branch. Update this PR directly rather than creating another PR.

@copilot Update #21241 directly with the following focused test simplifications. Preserve the production behavior and meaningful regression coverage. The target is the existing head repository open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation and branch copilot/fix-logback-mdc-export-isolation, retaining the stacked base copilot/java-agent-logback-change. Keep the branch assigned by GitHub Copilot cloud agent; do not rename it or create a replacement branch. If GitHub creates a platform-assigned follow-up branch, keep that branch. Update this PR directly rather than creating another PR.

In instrumentation/logback/logback-appender-1.0/library/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/logback/appender/v1_0/OpenTelemetryAppenderMdcExportTest.java, remove preservesApplicationSpanAndFlagsWhenEnrichmentUsesCustomizedKeys. Its original/application MDC values and exported/application-event assertions are already covered by exportsOriginalMdcAndDeliversEnrichedMdcAsynchronously in the existing asyncAppenderTest suite. Retain that async custom-key collision coverage, including original application span/flags/baggage values, absence of the enrichment-only trace attribute from export, and enriched application output.

Combine preservesApplicationMdcWhenCustomizedTraceIdKeyIsPresent and preservesApplicationOwnedEnrichmentKeys into one parameterized test over default versus customized trace/span/flags keys. Keep a real current span and baggage, put application-owned values under the configured trace/span/flags and baggage keys, and assert exact export of those original values. Both existing tests take the MDC appender's early return when its configured trace-id key is already present. Use wildcard MDC selection for this combined test and remove the wildcard-versus-explicit-selector dimension here, because existing selector tests cover matching. Keep the doesNotExportEnrichmentWithoutApplicationMdc cases unchanged.

Reduce exportsOnlyApplicationMdc from the six ordering/replay combinations to four meaningful scenarios: immediate export before enrichment, immediate export after enrichment, immediate export nested under the MDC appender, and replay with the exporter before enrichment. Preserve exact exported application-MDC assertions and enriched application-event assertions for these scenarios. The replay-before case must still queue the original event before enrichment and emit only original application values after enrichment and producer MDC clearing. Do not replace it with replay-after or replay-nested. Keep the setup readable and do not introduce a new test framework or unnecessary abstractions.

In instrumentation/logback/logback-appender-1.0/library/src/asyncAppenderTest/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/logback/appender/v1_0/AsyncOpenTelemetryAppenderTest.java, simplify exportsOriginalMdcAndDeliversEnrichedMdcAsynchronously. Keep producerFinished as the deterministic gate in asyncOutputAppender, so the worker processes the event only after the producer scopes end and producer MDC is cleared/changed. Replace the custom ListAppender subclass with a plain ListAppender, removing its redundant second producerFinished wait and applicationEventProcessed latch. Keep worker order applicationAppender.doAppend(event) then exporter.doAppend(event), and use testing.waitAndAssertLogRecords as the completion synchronization before inspecting applicationAppender.list. Retain exact exported attributes, enriched application output, teardown, and the existing downstream-AsyncAppender trace-correlation limitation. Do not add sleeps or new trace propagation.

Keep all three MdcContextTest unit tests, preservesLoggerContextProperties, and both starter exportsOnlyApplicationMdc configurations unchanged. Do not modify production code, dependencies, suite/version coverage, parent #21223, or unrelated tests as part of this cleanup.

Apply the narrowest applicable spotlessApply tasks directly before behavioral validation. Run the focused library MDC export test at baseline/latest dependencies and the existing asyncAppenderTest suite where feasible, following repository conventions. Acceptance is the four requested simplifications with preserved original-MDC isolation, custom-key collision coverage, replay-before mutation coverage, and deterministic async coverage.

[General] After enrichment, application mutations to the event MDC are ignored during export: removing or redacting `token` in a downstream appender filter still exports its original value, and newly added keys are omitted. Distinguish OpenTelemetry enrichment writes from application mutations so export reflects subsequent application additions, updates, and removals without capturing enrichment. Add a regression test that modifies the event MDC between enrichment and export.
